title.narrative: Jordan Inclusive, Transparent and Climate Responsive Investments Program For Results

description.narrative: Improve accountability to foster climate responsive investments and growth.

The development objective of the Inclusive, Transparent, and Climate Responsive Investments Program for Results for Jordan is to improve accountability to foster climate responsive investments and growth, where: investment is defined as public and private investment; climate responsive investments refer to public sector and private sector opportunities in Jordan's nationally determined contribution (NDC) and measured by the measurement, reporting, and verification (MRV) system; and accountability rests on a framework of enhanced transparency and feedback loops that inform investment and policy decisions. Additional financing (AF) and restructuring is to improve the development effectiveness and fiscal sustainability of public investment, to scale up support to climate responsive public and private investment, including by leveraging green financing and climate finance, to promote job and business opportunities for women, and to strengthen government effectiveness and social accountability through participatory policy making based on data. Restructuring adjusts the program to policy shifts and institutional reorganization in the past year and scales up and improves the initial result framework across result areas: it supports in particular targeted investment incentives to promote women business opportunities provided under the new Investment Environment Law enacted at the end of 2022 and its subsidiary legislation in February 2023, and promotes business and job opportunities for women in tourism in implementation of the tourism gender and inclusion plan which was an output of the parent program.

condition.narrative: 1. The Borrower shall vest the overall responsibility for the coordination, monitoring and evaluation of the Program in MOPIC, andto this end, MOPIC shall maintain at all times during Program implementation, with terms of reference, mandate, composition andresources satisfactory to the Bank, the Program Management Unit, to be responsible for: (i) the overall management, coordination,reporting, monitoring, and evaluation of Program implementation; (ii) hiring, and interfacing with independent verificationagencies, as needed; (iii) carrying out assessments of ministries and agencies implementation of Program activities; (iv)carrying out the technical audits; and (v) facilitating financial audits for the Program, all in accordance with the provisions ofthis Agreement and the Program Operational Manual.

2. The Borrower shall vest the overall responsibility for the coordination, monitoring and evaluation of the Program in MOPIC, andto this end, shall, though MOPIC, cause Ministry of Environment (“MOEnv”), in coordination with PMU, to be responsible for (i)coordination of the achievement of the Jordan's NDC under the Paris Agreement, (ii) establishment of relevant inter-ministerialgroups; and (iii) utilization of the National Climate Change Committee.

3. The Borrower shall, not later than three (3) months after the Effective Date, prepare an operational manual for the Program, inform and substance acceptable to the Bank, containing detailed (i) administrative, procurement, financial management and monitoringand evaluation procedures, (ii) environmental and social management systems and complaints and grievance redress mechanism, (iii)Program Action Plan; (iv) detailed arrangements for verification of achievement of the DLR (including the Verification Protocol);and (v) coordination and oversight arrangements for the Program.

title.narrative: Identifying private and non-government financing towards Jordan's NDC 2030 goals

baseline.value: 0% verifiable progress in mobilizing private sector climate investment towards the NDC goals

title.narrative: Enhancing Green and Climate Responsive Investments Towards Jordan's Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC) and Paris Agreement goals

baseline.value: Monitoring, Reporting & Verification (MRV) system piloted.Jordan performance on Climate Responsive Public Investment Management is rated D under its 2022 Climate Responsive Public Financial Management Performance Assessment Framework.No green sovereign bond issed by GoJ.0% in private sector and non-GOJ expenditure recorded in the MRV systemNo National Green Taxonomy in place.

target.value: Improved Jordan performance on Climate responsive Public Investment Management reflected by its rating B under the relevant indicator of the Climate Responsive Public Financial Management Framework (CRPFM 5).Sovereign green bond in Jordan is issued and National Green Taxonomy is adopted, with the intermediate milestones successfully achieved. Capacity in the green finance area of MOF, MOENV, and other stakeholders is enhanced.At least US$1.25billion cumulative progress recorded in MRV of private and non-GOJ climate finace.

comment.narrative: Achieving the NDC goals has two dimensions, (a) tracking climate finance from government, non-government and private sources and (b) tracking GHG emissions, emission reduction and adaptation/resilience co-benefits from activities across sectors. This indicator will assess progress in establishing the climate finance governance systems, which enables monitoring, verification and reporting of Jordan's progress towards NDC goals, through public and private sector investments.

actual.value: In progress

target.value: Improved Jordan performance on Climate responsive Public Investment Management reflected by its rating B under the relevant indicator of the Climate Responsive Public Financial Management Framework (CRPFM 5).Sovereign green bond in Jordan is issued and National Green Taxonomy is adopted, with the intermediate milestones successfully achieved. Capacity in the green finance area of MOF, MOENV, and other stakeholders is enhanced.At least US$1.25billion cumulative progress recorded in MRV of private and non-GOJ climate finace.

comment.narrative:
a) All public projects should be registered on the NRIP and already include a dedicated climate section in the PCN. Also, all public projects above $15m prepare a feasibility study that should include an environmental impact assessment.
b)Preparation for the issuance of Jordan's Sovereign Green Bond began in 2024 and is progressing. The Sovereign Green Bond Framework is now finalized, adopted, and published on MOF's website. A dedicated governmental working group was established and reviewed the required documentation, and exchanged technical inputs on the green bond scheme. Also, a pipeline of capital projects eligible for green bond financing has been finalized and categorized by priority. This task included screening budgets for around 25 entities and filtering those that met the criteria for green bond financing.
c) The Ministry of Environment provides capacity building support to national entities to enhance climate reporting through MRV system.

actual.value: In progress

title.narrative: Strengthening the Ministry of Investment's institutional focus on investment promotion and related investor services to attract quality investment.

baseline.value: There is a need to sharpen the focus of investment promotion and investor-servicing mandate and strengthen the systems used for implementation.

target.value: Increased investment facilitated, and more new jobs created, including as supported by gender-specific investment incentives.

comment.narrative: (a) Parliament enacts the new Investment Law; (b) the Council of Ministers adopts the corresponding Bylaw addressing the investment window under the new Investment Law; and (c) JIC adopts and publishes the Investment Promotion Strategy for CY21-24, including investment-specific KPIs: 1) Number of New Investment Decisions receiving investment facilitation services; 2) Number of investment projects receiving gender-related investment incentives in accordance with Article 13B of the Investment Environment Law and related bylaw; 3) Number of New Investment Started receiving investment facilitation services.

actual.value: In progress. Intermediate results 1, 3, and 4 related to the adoption of the Investment promotion strategy and the revision of two bylaws have been met. The Investment Promotion Strategy was adopted, and the CRM system has been operationalized. Awaiting reports generated from the CRM system to inform DLR achievement.

title.narrative: Strengthening the strategic direction and enhancing the regulatory environment of the tourism sector to foster high-quality private and public investment

baseline.value: Tourism potential is held back by a fragmented approach to sector development, regulatory constraints affecting private sector, underperforming public assets, which are being exacerbated by the COVID-19 impacts

target.value: The tourism sector strategic direction has been strengthened and regulatory environment enhanced; improvements in tourism sites leading to more tourists and higher tourist satisfaction; enhanced opportunities for training and employment for women in the tourism sector (approximately 800 beneficiaries expected).

comment.narrative:
Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities has adopted and published a National Tourism Strategy, and Gender and Inclusion Project Plan, both developed in consultation with tourism associations
MoTA has revised and adopted two out of the three (3) bylaws identified in the Verification Protocol to streamline and improve the tourism private sector enabling environment
Number of tourists tracked through the management information system in the sites that increased expenditure and adopted improved management plans (not yet measured).
Tourist satisfaction (measured through satisfaction surveys), in the sites that increased expenditure and adopted improved management plan (not yet measured).

actual.value: In progress. Intermediate targets 01 and 02 on the adoption of tourism bylaws have been met. DLR on Tourism bylaws has been fully achieved. The first Site Management Plan has been adopted (Amman Citadel). Substantial progress made with enhanced opportunities for training and employment for women in tourism sector.

title.narrative: Enhancing mobilization of green finance to generate climate-responsive investment

baseline.value: To address the existing climate financing gap, Jordan needs to further expand green finance markets and unlock additional sources climate-responsive finance.

target.value: Increased climate finance mobilization through the issuance of sovereign green bond; climate finance ecosystem facilitated by the adoption of the National Green Taxonomy; and enhanced capacity in the green finance area of MOF, MOENV, and other stakeholders.

comment.narrative: Achievement of all the major milestones in preparation of Jordan's first sovereign green bond and National Green Taxonomy.

actual.value: In progress. The Program achieved the intermediate indicators 4, 5, and 6 on operationalization of a working group for green bond preparation and issuance; Green bond integrated into the updated Debt Management Strategy; a comprehensive identification of eligible green investments has been completed; the Green Bond Framework is being reviewed by the Second Party Opinion provider. Draft National Green Taxonomy has been prepared and the open public consultation has been concluded.
